problems.title: A nineteenth-root equation
problems.question: How many real solutions satisfy ¹⁹√x=1/x⁹?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Exclude x=0 and raise both sides to the odd power 19.
steps: x=x^(−171), hence x¹⁷²=1.
The real candidates x=±1 both satisfy the original equation.

problems.title: Subtract an even function from itself
problems.question: f is even. Find the range of g(x)=f(x)−f(|x|).
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Evenness gives f(|x|)=f(x) for every input in the symmetric domain.
steps: Thus g(x)=0 everywhere it is defined.

problems.title: Area from angles and perimeter one
problems.question: A triangle has angles α,β,γ and perimeter 1. Express its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: By the sine rule, sides are ksinα,ksinβ,ksinγ with k=1/(sinα+sinβ+sinγ).
steps: Area=(1/2)(ksinα)(ksinβ)sinγ.
Substitute k².

problems.title: Distances from an interior point to three sides
problems.question: AB=10,AC=8,BC=6. Interior M is 2 from AC and 3 from BC. Find its distance to AB.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The 6-8-10 triangle is right; split its area into three triangles with vertex M.
steps: Total area=6·8/2=24. The pieces with bases AC,BC have areas 8·2/2=8 and 6·3/2=9.
The remaining area is 7=10d/2.

problems.title: A parabola visiting all four quadrants
problems.question: For which a does y=x²+ax+a−1 have points in all four quadrants?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The upward parabola already has positive values on both far ends; it needs negative values at both positive and negative x.
steps: Its negative interval must cross zero, which is equivalent to f(0)=a−1<0.
At a=1 a root is zero and negative values occur only for one sign of x.

problems.title: Exactly two true inequalities
problems.question: Which listed x makes exactly two of x²+7x−18<0, (x²+3x−4)/(x²+7x−30)<0, and 2|x−5|>8−x true?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Check candidates −15,−11,−8,−3,4,7: their numbers of true statements are 1,1,3,2,0,1.
Only −3 gives exactly two.

problems.title: Exactly two absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find a for which x²−(a+199)|x|+199a=0 has exactly two real roots.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Factor in t=|x|≥0: (t−199)(t−a)=0.
steps: t=199 always yields ±199. If a<0, the other t is invalid, leaving two roots.
If a=199 it duplicates that pair. If a=0 it adds zero; if a>0,a≠199 it adds two more roots.
problems.note: The printed option a<0 omits the valid exceptional value a=199; no printed option gives the full set.

problems.title: Greatest area from two medians
problems.question: Two triangle medians have lengths 6 and 9. Find the greatest possible area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The centroid triangle has sides 4 and 6 along these medians; its area is one third of the original.
steps: Original area=3·(1/2)·4·6 sinθ=36sinθ.
The maximum is attained when the medians are perpendicular.

problems.title: A rhombus cut by a diagonal and a line
problems.question: E lies on CD of rhombus ABCD with DE:EC=1:2. The B-angle bisector meets AE at M. Find area MBCE divided by area ABCD.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The bisector is diagonal BD. Ratios and area fractions can be computed in parallelogram coordinates.
steps: The shoelace formula gives area MBCE=(1/2)[5/4−1/3]=11/24 of the unit parallelogram.
An affine change preserves this area ratio for the actual rhombus.

problems.title: A sequence with equal five-term block sums
problems.question: The first three sequence terms are 1,3,19. Every five consecutive terms sum to 199. Find term 198.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Subtract two consecutive five-term sums to obtain aₙ₊₅=aₙ.
steps: The sequence repeats every five indices.
198 leaves remainder 3 modulo 5, so a₁₉₈=a₃.

problems.title: Greatest arithmetic difference containing three terms
problems.question: An arithmetic progression contains 2,11,17. Find the greatest possible common difference.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: A positive difference must divide both differences 11−2=9 and 17−2=15 into integer index steps.
steps: If 9=md and 15=nd, their greatest possible common step is gcd(9,15)=3.
The progression 2,5,8,11,14,17 attains it.

problems.title: Sum the tenth group of even numbers
problems.question: Even numbers are grouped with lengths 1,2,3,… . Find the sum in group 10.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Before group 10 there are 1+⋯+9=45 numbers.
steps: The group contains the 46th through 55th even numbers, namely 92 through 110.
Their sum is 10(92+110)/2.

problems.title: Arc length compared with chord length
problems.question: An arc and its chord have ratio 2π:3√3. Find the arc’s degree measure.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For angle θ in radians, arc/chord=θ/[2sin(θ/2)].
steps: This ratio increases strictly for 0<θ<2π, so the matching angle is unique.

problems.title: Areas of regular polygons on one circle
problems.question: Some vertices of a regular m-gon are the vertices of a regular n-gon, n<m. Find their area ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Both polygons have the same circumradius R; area of a regular k-gon=(k/2)R²sin(360°/k).
steps: Divide the m-gon formula by the n-gon formula and cancel R²/2.

problems.title: At least one head with probability above 0.9
problems.question: What is the fewest fair independent coin tosses for the probability of at least one head to exceed 0.9?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: P(at least one head)=1−2^(−n).
steps: Need 2ⁿ>10. Three tosses give 7/8=0.875; four give 15/16=0.9375.

problems.title: A difference bound for two random numbers
problems.question: Independent uniform x,y lie in [0,2]. Find P(|x−y|≤1).
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The sample square has area 4; its excluded parts are two right triangles of legs 1.
steps: Excluded area=2·(1/2)=1.
Allowed probability=(4−1)/4.

problems.title: Sum every third term starting at the second
problems.question: b₁=1,q=−1/2. Find b₂+b₅+b₈+⋯.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The selected terms form a geometric progression with first −1/2 and ratio q³=−1/8.

problems.title: Two pairs of perpendicular vectors
problems.question: Nonzero a⊥b and (a+2b)⊥(3a−b). Find |a|/|b|.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The dot product expands to 3|a|²−2|b|² because a·b=0.
steps: Set this equal to zero, giving |a|²/|b|²=2/3.
Take the positive square root.

problems.title: A minimum vector length
problems.question: a=(t+1,t+2), b=(t−1,t−2). For which t is |2a+3b| least?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Squared length=(5t−1)²+(5t−2)²=50(t−3/10)²+1/2.
The square is least at t=3/10.

problems.title: Recognize a geometric partial sum
problems.question: Which printed formula can give the sum of the first n terms of a geometric progression?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For Sₙ=3·3ⁿ−3=3(3ⁿ−1), the first term is 6 and common ratio is 3.
steps: The geometric formula 6(3ⁿ−1)/(3−1) gives exactly the printed expression.
Its consecutive differences are 6,18,54,… .
problems.note: If the option written 5n means 5 times n rather than 5 raised to n, it also describes a constant geometric progression with ratio 1. The source typography presents it as an exponential option.

problems.title: A prime satisfying a congruence
problems.question: How many three-digit primes x satisfy 2x+1≡x+1 mod199?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The congruence reduces to x≡0 mod199.
steps: The three-digit positive multiples are 199,398,597,796,995.
Only 199 is prime; all other multiples have a factor 199 and a factor greater than 1.

problems.title: Least mean with a prescribed unique mode and range
problems.question: Five natural numbers have unique mode 5 and range 5. Find the least possible mean.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The number 5 must occur at least twice. Minimize the remaining entries while preserving a unique mode.
steps: With minimum 1, the maximum is 6. With two 5s, the remaining smallest distinct entry is 2, since a second 1 would tie the mode. This gives (1,2,5,5,6), sum19.
Three or more 5s give at least sum22. If the minimum is at least2, the sum cannot improve on19.
Thus the minimum mean is 19/5.

problems.title: Equation of a rhombus incircle
problems.question: Find the incircle of the quadrilateral with vertices (0,0),(3,4),(8,4),(5,0).
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: All sides have length 5, so this is a rhombus. Its center is the intersection of diagonals.
steps: The center is midpoint of (0,0),(8,4), namely (4,2).
Its distances to y=0,y=4 are2; distance to side 4x−3y=0 is |16−6|/5=2 as well.

problems.title: Cosine between a line and the y-axis
problems.question: A=(1,1),B=(−3,−4). Find the cosine of the acute angle between AB and the y-axis.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: A direction vector is (4,5), with length √41.
steps: Its dot product with vertical unit vector (0,1) is5.
Divide by the vector length.

problems.title: Least distance from a hyperbola’s center
problems.question: A=(1,3), B lies on y=(3x−1)/(x−1). Find the least AB.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Translate coordinates u=x−1,v=y−3, giving uv=2.
steps: Distance squared is u²+v²≥2|uv|=4.
Equality occurs at u=v=√2 or u=v=−√2, both on the hyperbola.
